title: Mango Processing & Waste-to-Wealth Models
subtitle: Two replicable cases for Andhra Pradesh districts: the Philippines dried mango export cluster and the Malihabad Dasheri FPO processing cluster
audience: For district and mandal officers — horticulture, SHGs, FPOs and MSMEs

hero_stats.label: Mango produced annually in Andhra Pradesh, India's largest producer
Pulp units already running in the Chittoor–Tirupati cluster
Of the fruit becomes peel, kernel and scutcher — monetisable by-product

sections.title: Why Mango Processing Matters for Andhra Pradesh Districts
sections.lead: Andhra Pradesh is the largest mango producer in India, with over 31 lakh MT produced annually across Chittoor, Vizianagaram, Kadapa, Anantapur and Srikakulam. Yet only a fraction is processed — the rest is sold as fresh fruit at volatile prices or lost to gluts, pests and post-harvest spoilage. Processing converts that risk into income.

items.title: Shelf-life
items.body: Processing converts perishable mango into pulp, slice, pickle and amchur with a 12–24 month shelf life.

items.title: Waste-to-wealth
items.body: 35–60% of the mango is peel and kernel, which can become pectin, mango butter and animal feed.

items.title: Women and SHGs
items.body: Processing creates cottage-level slicing, pickling, packaging and grading jobs for women SHGs.

items.title: Local value
items.body: Pulp, pickle and brand value stay inside the mandal or cluster, not just the metropolis.

sections.kicker: CASE STUDY 1 — PHILIPPINES DRIED MANGO EXPORT CLUSTER
sections.title: A Brand-Led Export Model
sections.lead: Profood International Corporation, founded by Justin Uy in Cebu, has grown into the largest Philippine-based dried fruit producer, employing more than 8,000 workers across its factories. The cluster spans Cebu for branding and packaging and Mindanao for farm sourcing, turning a seasonal tropical fruit into a year-round branded export category sold in more than 60 countries.

items.label: Countries buying the cluster's branded mango products

blocks.label: Why it is relevant for AP
blocks.text: It shows how a single fruit category can be scaled into a branded export industry, and demonstrates contract-farming plus centralised processing discipline. AP's Chittoor already has 45 pulp units — the next step is brand and retail-pack.

sections.title: From Farm to Export Shelf
sections.lead: The Profood model is a four-stage chain that converts a perishable fruit into a 24-month-shelf-life branded export SKU.

items.title: Contract farming clusters
items.body: Profood ties up with mango growers in Mindanao for off-take at pre-agreed prices, ensuring steady raw material supply and farmer income stability through the six-month harvest window.

items.title: IPM and GlobalGAP certification
items.body: Farms follow Integrated Pest Management with fruit-bagging, residue testing and traceability. Certification unlocks export to the US, EU, Japan and Korea, where residue limits are tight.

items.title: Centralised processing plant
items.body: The Cebu plant handles washing, peeling, slicing, osmotic dehydration and freeze-drying, metal detection and nitrogen-flush packaging — one site, one quality standard, year-round output.

items.title: Brand and multi-channel export
items.body: Branded products ship to more than 60 countries via supermarket chains, duty-free shops and e-commerce. Brand margin is three to five times higher than bulk pulp.

sections.kicker: CASE STUDY 2 — MALIHABAD DASHERI CLUSTER, UTTAR PRADESH
sections.title: FPO-Led Processing Under the NHB Cluster Programme
sections.lead: Malihabad block in Lucknow district is the home of the Dasheri mango. Under the NHB Cluster Development Programme, the cluster has organised Farmer Producer Companies for collective raw-material aggregation, processing, branding and export. In June 2025, Malihabad Mango FPC and IRADA FPC dispatched a trial Dasheri shipment to Dubai.

items.label: Malihabad Mango FPC and IRADA FPC
Trial Dasheri export to Dubai dispatched

blocks.label: Why it is relevant for AP
blocks.text: It demonstrates that even without ocean-port access, an FPO can run a pickle and pulp cluster profitably, shows how the NHB Cluster Development Programme can be leveraged — the same scheme is open to AP — and the domestic and Gulf export market is accessible to AP's Chittoor and Vizianagaram clusters.

sections.title: FPO-Led Aggregation and Processing
sections.lead: The chain runs from grower to market: small and marginal farmers in cluster villages feed a Farmer Producer Company that aggregates raw fruit and runs a common brand; a pickle, pulp or slice processing unit owned or leased by the FPC and FSSAI-licensed does the conversion; NHB, KVK and CFTRI provide recipes, IPM, packaging and certification support; and produce moves through APMC wholesale, retail pouches and Gulf export channels.

blocks.label: Funding and scheme support
blocks.text: The NHB Cluster Development Programme, PMFME capital subsidy, NABARD credit and MoFPI cold chain support stack together.

blocks.label: The standard FPO processing unit package
blocks.text: An indicative package for a one MT per day pickle and pulp FPO unit: a 1,500–2,000 sq ft shed, stainless-steel washing and sorting tables, two pulpers, a paste mill and mixer, three jacketed tanks, a retort or pasteuriser for RTS beverage, a pouch-sealing and labelling machine, two cold storage chests, crates, drums and a basic lab kit, plus the FSSAI licence, packaging artwork and brand mark.

blocks.label: Indicative capex
blocks.text: Rs 18–25 lakh per unit before the 35% PMFME subsidy; working capital Rs 8–10 lakh per season.

sections.title: Every Component Gets a Use
sections.lead: During industrial mango processing, 35–60% of the fruit becomes by-product — peel, kernel, scutcher and sap. Peer-reviewed research confirms these are rich in pectin, polyphenols, carotenoids and arachidic acid, all monetisable.

items.title: Peel
items.body: Pectin extraction, polyphenol and carotenoid extract, dietary fibre, natural colourant and compost.

items.title: Kernel
items.body: Mango butter for cosmetics, edible oil rich in arachidic acid, animal feed and starch.

items.title: Scutcher and fibre
items.body: Animal feed, compost, vermi-compost and bio-pellets or fuel.

items.title: Sap and latex
items.body: Traditional dye base, adhesive and medicinal or herbal use.

blocks.label: The working principle
blocks.text: Localise bulky primary processing — pulp, peel-drying, kernel crushing — at cluster level; centralise advanced extraction of pectin, mango butter and polyphenols at district or state level where capital and lab capacity exist.

sections.title: From Bulk Pulp to Branded Diversification
sections.lead: Andhra Pradesh already has one of India's largest mango processing clusters — about 45 pulp units, 36 in Chittoor and 9 in Tirupati, processing mainly Totapuri into pulp for export to West Asia. Recent geopolitical disruption left around 3 lakh tonnes of pulp stranded, pointing to the need for product diversification, branding and domestic retail channels.

blocks.label: The impact pathway
blocks.text: The farmer earns a stable off-take price via FPO contract rather than only the APMC spot price. SHG-run pickle, slice and pulp units generate 30–50 jobs per cluster. Peel and kernel return to farming as compost or are sold as pectin and butter feedstock, and brand plus retail-pack captures three to five times the margin of bulk pulp export.

blocks.label: The message for AP
blocks.text: Review each mango cluster not only for area and production but also for processing potential and by-product monetisation. The stranded-pulp crisis of 2024 is the argument for diversification.

sections.kicker: LESSONS FOR AP DISTRICT AND MANDAL OFFICIALS
sections.title: Six Lessons That Translate Directly
sections.lead: The Philippines and Malihabad cases converge on six lessons that sequence what to do first, what to standardise and what to measure — so that machinery purchase does not precede market and raw-material readiness.

items.title: Start with clusters
items.body: Select mango-dense mandals in Chittoor, Tirupati, Vizianagaram and Kadapa so raw-material aggregation is viable. A cluster of 1,000 ha within a 25 km radius is the minimum viable unit.

items.title: Keep first processing local
items.body: Bulky mango fruit cannot travel long distances economically. Pulp, slice, pickle and amchur should be processed within 30 km of harvest to cut losses and retain local jobs.

items.title: Use SHGs and FPOs
items.body: Women SHGs and farmer FPOs are the ideal operators for pickle, slice, amchur and cottage pulp units. The FPO structure gives aggregation, working capital and brand identity.

items.title: Standardise products
items.body: Recipes, packaging, labels, the FSSAI licence, batch tracking and quality control are non-negotiable. Without them there is no retail shelf, no export order and no repeat buyer.

items.title: Converge schemes
items.body: Horticulture, DRDA and SHG support, the PMFME 35% capital subsidy, APEDA export support, MSME credit, the NHB cluster programme and KVK technical support — stack, do not silo.

items.title: Track outcomes
items.body: Measure income to farmers, jobs created, MT processed and sold, repeat buyers and export value, in a monthly review by the Joint Director of Horticulture and the DRDA Project Director.

sections.kicker: HOW AP DISTRICTS CAN ADAPT THE MODELS
sections.title: Three Parallel Tracks
sections.lead: Fresh mango processing, by-product monetisation and district-level enablers should run together. The aim is to convert Chittoor and Vizianagaram from bulk-pulp clusters into branded, diversified mango hubs.

items.title: Fresh mango processing
items.body: Convert the harvest into branded SKUs: pulp in aseptic drums and retail pouches, slice and IQF for HoReCa and QSR chains, SHG-led pickle, amchur for the spice trade, candy and bars for school and tourism retail, and RTS beverage and nectar.

items.title: By-product monetisation
items.body: Turn 35–60% of the fruit into revenue: peel to pectin and polyphenol extract at district level, kernel to mango butter at cluster and central level, scutcher to animal feed and vermi-compost at village level, and compost returned to the mango orchard to close the loop.

items.title: District-level enablers
items.body: A district mango value-chain map and cluster atlas, technical tie-ups with KVK, NRCB, CFTRI and IIHR, a common AP brand with FSSAI hand-holding and a packaging kit, buyer linkages with retail chains and APEDA buyers, the PMFME subsidy and bank credit stack, and a monthly Horticulture and DRDA KPI review.

blocks.label: The ideal first step
blocks.text: Identify one mango cluster per district and run a 100-day pilot — one pulp and pickle FPO unit, one brand, one buyer tie-up — before scaling.

sections.title: What to Review Every Month
sections.lead: A monthly KPI review by the Joint Director of Horticulture and the DRDA Project Director keeps the mango cluster on track, in three tiers.

items.title: Input and process KPIs
items.body: Mango farmers, SHGs and FPOs mobilised; fruit aggregated in MT; trainees completing practical training; FSSAI and APEDA registrations completed; unit utilisation and days of operation; and hectares under IPM and GlobalGAP practice.

items.title: Output KPIs
items.body: Pulp, pickle, slice and amchur produced and sold with value realised; SKUs and brands launched; peel and kernel sent for by-product use; compost returned to farms; and export shipments dispatched.

items.title: Outcome KPIs
items.body: Additional income to farmers and SHGs; jobs created for women and rural youth; reduction in post-harvest loss; repeat buyers and market expansion; brand premium captured over the bulk-pulp price; and cluster-level mango price stabilisation against the APMC spot.

blocks.label: The closing message
blocks.text: For district and mandal officials, the mango case studies show how a crop-specific value chain can move from production monitoring to income, enterprise and employment generation. The Philippines case proves branding scales a single fruit into a global category; Malihabad proves an FPO cluster can run a profitable pickle, pulp and amchur mix. AP's Chittoor and Vizianagaram clusters have the raw material — they need the brand, the FPO discipline and the by-product line.
